newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols firm, eyes on short dates.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols firm, eyes on short dates.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-mark options bounced after steadily declining in recent weeks as the spot dollar broke above the 1.75-mark level to a fresh 40-month high of 1.7550, dealers said.
Sterling/dollar volatilities inched up in the wake of a roller-coaster ride in spot cable after the U.K. budget announcement, while dollar/yen volatilities continued eroding.

Traders noted that the market showed little reaction to news that the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) because the decision had been widely anticipated.

The dollar/mark rally early on wiped out a large amount of exotic options with a barrier price at 1.75 marks, prompting market-makers to cover their short-gamma hedge positions and pushing up front-end volatilities, traders said.
"It's a continuation of the slow, grinding move we've had for the last month, but we've come to a critical level," a U.S. bank trader in New York said.

More than $1 billion of Monday expiries were said to have traded in the past two days, and some traders linked them to gamma demand stemming from the ill-fated exotic options that disappeared today. Shorter-dated options have higher gamma.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark rose to 8.4/8.6 percent from 7.9/8.2 late on Tuesday. The curve stayed slightly positively sloped, with one-year bid marginally higher at 9.1/9.3 percent.
Some traders said the bounce in dollar/mark volatilities looked tentative and might not mean there was growing anticipation of a breakaway dollar rally.

"I think people are still in the process of adjusting their positions now," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York. "When the dust settles, we'll see if the landscape has changed dramatically."

In sterling, one-month cable volatility edged up 0.1 point after the budget announcement to 7.4/7.7 percent. One-month sterling/mark was off early highs at 9.2/9.6 percent, but up a quarter point on the day.
"Sterling's been whipping around today," a hedge fund trader said.
Activity was slowing down in most currencies by early afternoon U.S., but but traders noted that a huge amount of options expire on Thursday, keeping the market nervous.
"I think people are going to be working on their expirations tomorrow," the hedge fund trader said.

The expirations, particularly of exotic options with barrier prices near 110 yen, might help resolve the prolonged extreme skews in dollar/yen risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, Okada at DKB said.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal has so far shown little signs of relenting, quoted at 2.2/2.6 points in favor of yen calls, even though spot has stayed above 114 yen this week.
While end-user demand remains strong, expiration of the exotics should help normalize the volatile downside gamma exposure changes for some market-makers, Okada said.
One-month yen volatility was flat at 9.9/10.1 percent.
